title: Noir you can finish tonight
blurb: Ten films under ninety minutes from the years when the studios shot fast and cheap and the shadows did the acting. Start with Detour if you have never seen a noir: sixty-eight minutes, six days of shooting, and one of the bleakest endings in American film.

films.note: Shot in six days. Nobody in it is having a good time, and it's perfect.
A man walks into a police station to report his own murder.
Ida Lupino directing: two men, one gun, a long desert road.

A bag of money lands in the back seat. Lizabeth Scott decides to keep it.
Fritz Lang, Edward G. Robinson, and a painting that ruins everyone.
Orson Welles as a Nazi hiding in a Connecticut town.
The procedural that became Dragnet, shot in the LA storm drains.
A wife hunts for the husband who ran from a murder he witnessed.
Mickey Rooney borrows twenty dollars from the till. It gets worse.
